articles.title: Historic With-Browning Telescope with Unique Provenance
articles.summary: The article details Robert A. Garfinkle's acquisition of a historic 1874 With-Browning reflector telescope, notable for its unique provenance. This instrument was previously owned by prominent English lunar observers, including Edmund Neison, Thomas Gwyn Elger, Walter Goodacre, and Hugh Percy Wilkins, and was even used by Sir Patrick Moore. Garfinkle describes the telescope's specifications, its recent appraisal and resilvering, and his plans to restore its base and extensively research its rich history.

articles.title: The Celestial Tourist Speaks
articles.summary: Jay Reynolds Freeman recounts his extensive amateur astronomy journey, having logged over 10,000 unique celestial objects and more than 22,000 observations since 1978. He details his primary observing instruments, particularly his Celestron 14, and discusses his systematic approach using guides like Burnham's Celestial Handbook and the Millennium Star Atlas. Freeman expresses his enduring passion for discovering new and challenging deep-sky objects and ponders future observing endeavors.

articles.title: Auction XXI
articles.summary: The article reports on the successful 'Auction XXI' fundraising event, which generated over $1000 for the organization. It also highlights the robust School Star Party program, noting 25 successful events and good turnouts even for later 'after-DST' sessions, extending the program's reach. Additionally, it announces an upcoming public lecture by distinguished astronomer Dr. Vera Rubin on galaxies and dark matter at Foothill College.

articles.title: The Buzz on Petau, Kopernik and Tyge
articles.summary: This article details the advantages of observing the early Moon high in the sky during certain times of the year, particularly focusing on craters like Petavius, Copernicus, and Tycho, and how this offers excellent twilight viewing opportunities. The author recounts a memorable experience viewing the complex rille structure in Petavius under superb atmospheric conditions. It also delves into the historical and political influences behind the Latinized naming conventions of various lunar features.

articles.title: AANC Conference Scrapbook
articles.summary: The article provides a 'scrapbook' recap of the AANC Conference held at Chabot Space & Science Center in Oakland on April 7th, attended by 105 people from 27 AANC groups, including an SJAA presentation. It features photos of notable attendees and an award presentation. Additionally, it includes an observing guide for May, advising on viewing Jupiter and Saturn, and emphasizing early practice for observing Mars ahead of its mid-June opposition.

articles.title: Seth Shostak to Speak at May 5th General Meeting
articles.summary: Seth Shostak, Public Programs Scientist at the SETI Institute, is scheduled to speak at the May 5th general meeting. His talk, "The Chances for Finding E.T.," will explore new developments in SETI science and technology, as well as the societal implications and public announcement process if a signal is discovered. Shostak, also an author, will have copies of his book available at the event.

articles.title: SJAA Loaner Scope Status
articles.summary: The SJAA Loaner Scope Status document details the availability of telescopes for members of the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA). It provides lists of scopes currently available for immediate loan, those recently loaned out with due dates, and scopes on extended loan. Members can contact Mike Koop to borrow a scope, and the document also mentions recent donations to the loaner program.
